items.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022
items.q: I loved Billy Higgins though too.

ctx.x: because I’m not playing that kind of music that much. You know when the drummer sneaks in? You know when you’re playing and you sneak in soft-soft-soft-soft. He never heard that man. He flipped over it. And after a while he’d go, [whispers] “Sneak in, sneak in,” you know while he’s on stage. You know I wouldn’t be playing and he’d go “Sneak in, sneak in, man, sneak in.” And then just soft cymbal, just soft cymbal, and even no hi- hat man. Then all of a sudden a little hi-hat, maybe cross stick you know. He went…
Who were your biggest influences in terms of drummers?

Oh man, well Philly Joe really and “Billy Boy” man, you know, listen to that one. What’s wrong with that? “Billy Boy” man. And Art Blakey man, in the very beginning Art Blakey was just thundering. And Kenny Clarke man. Brushes? Kenny Clarke, what a player man. I loved Billy Higgins though too. Billy Higgins. And Buddy. I was on the phone with Frank DeVito last night, my cousin who is a drummer from Utica and he’s like 90 now, 91. We were talking about, every once in a while we talk about Buddy Rich. You have to.
